problemStatement.plain: For finite subsets of Z with at least 2 elements, the edge boundary has at least 2 elements. Intervals achieve this bound.
whyMatters: Discrete analogue of the classical isoperimetric inequality
Foundation for higher-dimensional discrete isoperimetric theorems

currentState.nextAction: Higher-dimensional case (ℤ^d via Bollobás–Leader compression) is the natural follow-up.

knowledge.progressSummary: VERIFIED: 1D discrete isoperimetric inequality on ℤ — for finite S with |S| ≥ 2, |∂S| ≥ 2; equality on intervals. 0 axioms, 0 sorries.
builtItems: edgeBoundary definition for Finset ℤ via shift-image difference
insights: Min/max endpoints of a Finset ℤ furnish a canonical pair of distinct boundary witnesses (m-1 and M+1) without needing connectivity or interval structure
|S| ≥ 2 is consumed exactly once, via Finset.min_lt_max_of_card, which forces the two witnesses to be distinct
Equality on intervals reduces to a 4-way case analysis on the membership characterization (x+1 vs x-1 lands inside [a,b]; x is or is not in [a,b]); linarith handles all branches uniformly
Vertex-boundary formulation ((S.image (·-1)) ∪ (S.image (·+1))) \ S avoids needing a separate edge type and keeps everything in Finset ℤ
nextSteps: Extend to ℤ^d via Bollobás–Leader compression
Prove uniqueness of equality (|∂S| = 2 ⇒ S is an interval)
Formalize Harper theorem on the discrete hypercube {0,1}^n
Quantitative stability: bound symmetric difference to nearest interval when |∂S| ≤ 2 + ε
